message.content:
`docker start` is **not** the command to bring up the Docker daemon (the “Docker Engine”).  
It’s used to start *running* containers that have already been created.  
To get Docker running on a Windows machine you need to start the Docker service (or the Docker Desktop application), not a container.

---

## Starting the Docker Engine (service)

If you’re running Docker Engine on Windows Server or a Windows machine that has the Docker service installed, you can start it from PowerShell or CMD:

```powershell
# PowerShell – start the Docker service
Start-Service Docker
```

or

```cmd
rem CMD – start the Docker service
net start Docker
```

If you prefer the Service Control Manager syntax:

```cmd
sc start Docker
```

> **Tip:** If you’re using Docker Desktop on Windows 10/11, the Docker service is usually named `com.docker.service`. You can start it with:

```cmd
sc start com.docker.service
```

---

## Starting Docker Desktop (GUI)

On Windows 10/11, Docker Desktop is a desktop application. The simplest way to start it is:

1. Click the **Start** button → type “Docker Desktop” → press **Enter** (or click the icon).
2. Alternatively, run the executable directly (usually located at `C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe`):

```powershell
& "C:\Program Files\Docker\Docker\Docker Desktop.exe"
```

Once Docker Desktop launches, it will automatically start the underlying Docker service (`com.docker.service`) and you’ll see the whale icon in the system tray turn green.

---

## What `docker start` actually does

After Docker is running, you can start individual containers with:

```bash
docker start <container_name_or_id>
```

For example, to start a container named `my_web_app`:

```bash
docker start my_web_app
```

This command only works if the Docker daemon is already running.

---

### Summary

| Task | Command |
|------|---------|
| Start Docker Engine (service) | `Start-Service Docker` (PowerShell) or `net start Docker` (CMD) |
| Start Docker Desktop (app) | Launch `Docker Desktop.exe` from the Start menu or run it directly |
| Start an existing container | `docker start <container>` |

If you try to run `docker start` before the Docker daemon is up, you’ll get an error like “Cannot connect to the Docker daemon.” So make sure the service or Docker Desktop is running first.
